# Settings by pair, timeframe and session

// Hand-maintained guide for tools/cisd-ultimate-balanced.pine. The per-timeframe table in section 2 is
// generated by `python3 tools/tf-scale-table.py` - regenerate it, do not retype it. This file is the
// artifact behind a standing instruction: whenever an input is added, renamed or re-defaulted, this file
// and section 5 of tools/cisd-v1-guide.md change in the same commit.

## 0. The question this file answers

Two related ones.

*Does the indicator adapt when I switch timeframes?* Partly by construction, now more by rule, and there
is a residual set that no script can guess for you. Section 1 splits those three buckets.

*What should I be using on this pair, at this hour?* Section 3 through 5. Short version: the defaults are
tuned for a **5-minute EURUSD/GBPUSD chart**, and every number in the file that is a *bar count* was
silently assuming that chart. They no longer are.

## 1. Three buckets: automatic, derived, still yours

**Automatic regardless of any setting.** Anything measured in minutes or NY hours, because those are
absolute time and not bar counts: the killzone blocks (`timeMode`, `kz_london`, `kz_ny`, `kz_asia`,
`kz_loncls`, `kz_nypm`, `use_killzones`), the Silver Bullet and macro marks (`useSb`, `useMacro`), the
after-hours cutoff (`stopHour`), the opening range (`useOR`, `orLenMin`, `orSweepA/B`), the killzone level
pool (`kzl_s_asia`, `kzl_s_london`, `kzl_s_nyam`, `kzl_s_loncls`, `kzl_s_nypm`, `kzlPdhPd`, `kzlProject`,
`kzlMitigate`, `kzlMaxLive`, `kzlDrawLabels`, `kzlShade`): the pooled windows are this file's five `w*`
minute blocks, not a second set of times, so London and NY AM move with `Killzone set` and with nothing else), and the whole CRT
clock (`crtAnchorH`, `crtAnchorLen`, `crtWinOpen`, `crtWinLen`, `crtDeliverH`, `crtCbdrMax`'s 14:00-20:00
window, `crtAsiaMax`'s 20:00-00:00 window). Switch from 5m to 1H and these mean exactly what they meant
before, which is the correct behaviour - 01:00 New York is 01:00 New York.

**Derived from the chart now, under the new default.** The preset ladder (`tolerence`, `len`,
`min_score_for_best`, `signal_cooldown`, `atr_mult_sl`, `near_atr_mult`, `max_fvgs_per_side`,
`max_obs_per_side`) is selected by the chart's timeframe, and the bar-count parameters the ladder never
covered are rescaled to hold their *duration* still: `expiry_bars`, `liquidity_lookback`,
`clean_after_bars`, `ifvgAge`, `crtObAge`, plus three values that used to be literals buried in the code -
the FVG freshness window (10 bars), the order-block freshness window (12), the 25-bar premium/discount
range, and the killzone level layer's session minimum (`kzlMinBars`).

**Still yours, on any pair, at any timeframe.** `pipSz`-denominated caps, the session you trade, your
key levels, news times, the SMT sibling symbol, the killzone level **windows** if you fill them in - they are
empty by default precisely so this bucket stays empty, and an index CFD whose Asia really is 19:00-23:00 on
your feed should say so there rather than in a re-tuned `expiry_bars` - and where the dashboard sits
(`Dashboard position`), which is a chart-layout question that used to be answered for you, whether the CRT layer is on at all (`crtOn`, default
**off**), and whether the killzone level layer is (`kzlOn`, default **off**). See section 4.

## 2. What "auto" actually picks

`preset` is now `Auto from chart | 3min | 5min | 15min | 30min | 60min | 240min | 1D | Custom`, with
`Auto from chart` the default. Auto reads `timeframe.in_seconds()` and walks this ladder: <=180s `3min`,
<=300 `5min`, <=900 `15min`, <=1800 `30min`, <=3900 `60min`, <=15000 `240min`, else `1D`.

Two properties worth knowing before you trust it:

*It selects, it does not interpolate.* The tiers are hand-tuned per timeframe by the source material, and
they are **not** linear in time (5m and 15m disagree about the direction of several parameters). So Auto
maps your chart onto the nearest tuned tier instead of inventing an in-between value. A 20-minute chart
gets the `30min` tier and the scaling appropriate to 20 minutes; nothing averages those.

*The coarse tiers are my extrapolation, not tuning.* `60min`, `240min` and `1D` did not exist before, and
no source in this repository publishes a parameter table for them; they extend the observed trend of the
fine tiers. Nothing at 1H and above has been backtested. The panel's first row shows
`<tier> / <chart period> x<scale>` and both BEST alerts carry the tier, so the assumption is visible on
the chart rather than hidden in a default.

The rescaling rule, in full, is `scale = 300 / timeframe.in_seconds()` and each window becomes
`max(3, round(ref x scale))`, except the premium/discount range which is `max(8, round(25 x scale))`.
`Custom` turns the rescaling off entirely and uses every input as written. **Picking a named tier changes
only the ladder** - the windows keep following the chart, which is the point: on a 30m chart you can force
15-minute scoring without getting 5-minute windows back.

### The numbers, generated

```
| chart | tier it picks | scale | expiry | liq look | clean after | iFVG age | CRT / OB age | FVG / OB fresh | prem-disc | KZL session min | expiry as time | clean as time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1m | `3min` | x5 | 300 | 60 | 175 | 900 | 60 | 50 / 60 | 125 | 30 | 5.0 h | 2.9 h |
| 3m | `3min` | x1.67 | 100 | 20 | 58 | 300 | 20 | 17 / 20 | 42 | 10 | 5.0 h | 2.9 h |
| 5m | `5min` | x1 | 60 | 12 | 35 | 180 | 12 | 10 / 12 | 25 | 6 | 5.0 h | 2.9 h |
| 15m | `15min` | x0.3333 | 20 | 4 | 12 | 60 | 4 | 3 / 4 | 8 | 3 | 5.0 h | 3.0 h |
| 30m | `30min` | x0.1667 | 10 | 3 | 6 | 30 | 3 | 3 / 3 | 8 | 3 | 5.0 h | 3.0 h |
| 60m | `60min` | x0.0833 | 5 | 3 | 3 | 15 | 3 | 3 / 3 | 8 | 3 | 5.0 h | 3.0 h |
| 4H | `240min` | x0.0208 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 4 | 3 | 3 / 3 | 8 | 3 | 12.0 h | 12.0 h |
| 1D | `1D` | x0.0035 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 / 3 | 8 | 3 | 72 h | 72 h |
```

Read the last two columns, not the middle ones, and treat `KZL session min` as a floor rather than a
setting: `kzlMinBars` (6 at 5m) is `f_sc`-scaled like every other bar count, and `f_sc` never goes below 3,
so a session has to span three bars to produce a level at all. That is fine from 1m to 30m. It bites at
1H, where the two-hour windows (London close, NY PM) are 2 bars and so never make levels, and it kills the
layer at 4H, where every session is one bar against a 3-bar floor. Run this layer on 1H or finer. Expiry is 5.0 hours on every timeframe from 1m to 60m -
that is the property the rescaling exists to buy. Where a row stops matching, a floor is holding it up:
at 4H every window is pinned at 3 bars (12 hours, not 5) and at 1D likewise (72 hours). Below
`300/timeframe` the arithmetic cannot express "a fifth of a bar", so the behaviour degrades to "a handful
of bars" and that is the honest boundary of the extrapolation. If you run 4H or 1D charts, expect to set
`expiry_bars`, `liquidity_lookback` and `ifvgAge` by hand with `preset = Custom`, and treat anything the
score says at those timeframes as unvalidated.

Two side effects of the 1m row, both intended but worth seeing: `ifvgAge` becomes 900 bars, which is the
input's ceiling, so the inverted-zone layer scans a quarter of a thousand bars per candidate; and
`liqLook` at 30m/1H floors at 3 bars, which is a thinner liquidity check than the 5m chart gets, not a
stronger one.

**One correction to section 2, found on 2026-10-12 (audit §16).** That table was, for one row, describing a
branch that did not exist: the ladder's `3min` rung read `tier == "%s"` after the rename, so a 1m/2m/3m chart
selected the tier, printed it, and applied nothing - `tolerence` 0.55, `len` 8, `signal_cooldown` 5,
`atr_mult_sl` 0.40, `near_atr_mult` 2.5 were unreachable. It is fixed, so the table is now true, and 1m-3m
charts get the faster filter set the ladder always said they should. That is the only change in this build
that is not behind a switch, because the switch (`preset = Auto`) was already nominally on.

## 3. What genuinely differs per pair

Everything size-related in this script is expressed either in **ticks** (`syminfo.mintick`) or in
**ATR multiples** (`tolerence`, `min_fvg_atr`, `near_mult_inp`, `atr_mult_sl_inp`, `ifvgDisp`,
`crtRangeMin/Max`). Both scale with the instrument by themselves; you do not touch them when you change
pair. The exceptions are all in one place:

| setting | unit it assumes | FX majors | JPY pairs | gold, indices, crypto |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pipSz` (internal) | 1 pip = 10 ticks, except 1 tick when the tick is 0.01 | correct | correct | wrong by 10x or more |
| `crtCbdrMax` (50) | pips | as written | as written | the number is in the wrong unit |
| `crtAsiaMax` (40) | pips | as written | as written | the number is in the wrong unit |
| `crtMinRiskT` (10) | ticks | ~1 pip, sensible | ~10 pips on 3-digit feeds, too big | fine but tiny in dollar terms |
| pip figures in labels and alerts | pips | fine | fine | mislabelled, decisions unaffected |

So on `XAUUSD`, `DEULX`/`US30`/`NQ`, or crypto the rule is: **disable the two pip caps (set them to 0) and
lean on the range-relative tests instead** - `crtAdrMult` (prior day range over 5-day average, a ratio,
unit-free), `crtRangeMin`/`crtRangeMax` (range over ATR, unit-free) and `crtTrendFrac`/`crtTightFrac`
(fractions). They measure the same thing the 2017 stand-aside list was measuring, without needing to know
what a pip means on your feed. If you would rather keep the pip caps, set them to the equivalent in *your*
broker's pip, which you can read off the chart in one step: Data Window, or `syminfo.mintick` on the
status line, then divide by 10 if your feed quotes 3 decimals for a JPY pair.

`crtMinRiskT` is the one to *raise* on cheap-tick instruments: a box whose stop is 10 ticks of a 0.01 gold
feed is 0.10, which sits inside a normal quote spread, so the whole "trade" is friction. That is
arithmetic and not a measurement: an earlier draft of this file quoted a -0.216R-after-friction figure
attributed to the audit, and no such study exists. It was removed from here, from the study's F9 row and
from the `crtMinRiskT` tooltip; see `tools/cisd-audit.md` section 15.

For `EURUSD` and `GBPUSD` nothing in section 3 needs changing, and `crtFri = Mark only`, `crtSA = on` and
both pip caps are the shipped defaults for a reason: they are the source's own numbers.

## 4. By session, for entries at the open

Your stated use case is iFVG entries at market open or at named hours. `ifvgWin` (take inverted entries
only inside the trading window) is on, `use_killzones` is on, and `kz_london` + `kz_ny` are on while
`kz_asia`, `kz_loncls` and `kz_nypm` are off. The published material in `concepts/` and the CRT sources
agree on the ordering; the row below is that agreement, not a measurement.

| session | what to set | why |
|---|---|---|
| London open, 02:00-05:00 NY | `kz_london` on, `kz_asia` off, `crtAnchorH` 1, `crtAnchorLen` 240 | the 01:00 NY 4H anchor, the 01:30 sweep in the screenshots, the 90-minute window |
| the hourly checkpoints (02:00 / 03:00 / 05:00 / 09:00 / 13:00) | `crtAnchorLen` 60 **and** `Anchor cadence` = `Every reference candle` | cadence at `Once per day` (the default) is one anchor per day; that is what the first build could do, and `crtAnchorLen` alone did not buy what its tooltip implied |
| New York open, 08:30-11:00 NY | `kz_ny` on, `useOR` on, `orGate` on if you want the 08:00 range as a pool | the 08:00 opening range and the 09:00-11:00 sweep window are already the defaults there |
| Asia | `kz_asia` on, and expect nothing | the CRT sources are blunt: manipulation ranges in Asia on 1m-5m charts carry near-zero edge; the honest setting is "watch, do not trade" |
| after 16:00 NY | leave `stopHour` 16 | one bar of thin session should not create a BEST label |

`crtWinLen` (90 minutes) is deliberately not a bar count, so the 01:00-02:30 sweep window survives a switch
from 5m to 15m intact. What does not survive a switch to a 4H chart is having anywhere to act: a
90-minute window is a third of one bar, so at best one candle is inside it. If you want the open-based
playbook, run the *chart* at 5m or 15m and let `crtAnchorLen` = 240 give you the 4H reference candle. That
is the split the screenshots use - a 15m execution chart reading a 4H range - and it is the one the
indicator is shaped for.

## 5. A starting point, per instrument

Marked as a starting point on purpose: no source in this repository validates a settings set, and the
win-rate claims around CRT (45% raw, 60-70% filtered) are self-reported and un-audited. What follows is the
configuration that matches how the models in `concepts/` are described, on a chart where the parameters were
tuned.

**FX majors, intraday, the default chart.** `preset = Auto from chart` on a 5m chart is a no-op against the
previous release - every derived window lands on the number the inputs already carried - so if 5m is your
only timeframe, nothing changes for you and the auto path costs you nothing to keep. Turn on
`require_liq_sweep`, `require_fvg`, `min_score_inp` 3, `crtOn` with `crtAnchorH` 1 / `crtAnchorLen` 240 /
`crtAccept = Close back inside`, `crtBias = HTF bias`, `crtOneShot` on, `crtSA` on. Leave `htf_tf` at 60, which is what the intraday bias in
the source material reads.

**The same model on 15m or 30m.** Change nothing but the chart. You get 15min/30min scoring and windows
of a third or a sixth of the bar count, which is the same elapsed time. Watch the panel's first row: it
should read `15min / 15 x0.3333`. If it does not, `timeframe.in_seconds()` is not what you think it is
(15m is 900) and you should tell me, because that is a bug and not a tuning question.

**Gold and the index CFDs.** Section 3's substitutions: `crtCbdrMax` 0, `crtAsiaMax` 0, `crtMinRiskT`
raised to a tenth of your ATR in ticks, `crtRangeMin` up to about 0.5 (a gold 4H range under 0.3 ATR is
noise), and `require_htf_bias` on because the counter-trend penalty in the sources is the largest reported
win-rate killer. Expect the 01:30 playbook to be about liquidity sweeps of the Asian range rather than the
daily open: gold's own open is not 08:00 NY, and this script does not know where it is - `useOR` is a
08:00-NY rule. If you turn on `kzlOn` here, read the `Add the prior day's high and low` tooltip before you
judge the two PDH/PDL lines: on a CME feed the daily bar is the Globex session, so those bounds are not what
a spot-FX chart would call yesterday's high and low - the discrepancy is the feed's day, and the level is
still a level.

**1H and above.** Use `preset = Custom` for the windows (the floors are doing more work than the scaling
there, section 2) and read `60min`/`240min`/`1D` as an extrapolation in the alerts, not a tuned tier.
Set `htf_tf` to `D` by hand. That single input is the one timeframe-dependent setting the script will not
derive: `request.security`'s timeframe argument has to be a constant or an input, and a chart-derived one
is a computed string that the TradingView editor may reject outright - a total failure (the script will not
paste) traded against a convenience, so it stays manual and the mapping is in the tooltip: 60 for 1m-5m,
240 for 15m, 480 for 30m, D for 1H and above.

The killzone level layer has a harder limit than tuning at coarse timeframes, and it is arithmetic: the
session-span guard is `f_sc(kzlMinBars)`, `f_sc` never goes below 3, and no session window in this file is
longer than four hours. At 1H that means the two-hour windows (London close, NY PM) can never make a level -
they are 2 bars against a floor of 3 - and at 4H *every* session is 1 bar, so the layer runs, counts, draws
nothing and stays silent in the alerts. 30m and finer is where it belongs; above that, read `KZL levels` in
the panel as "0 live / 0 made" and know which of the two you are looking at.

## 6. Keeping this file true

The rule, so the next change does not silently strand it:

1. New or renamed input, or a new default: update the bucket list in section 1 and the affected row of
   section 3, 4 or 5. If the input is a bar count, it belongs in section 2's scaling and in
   `tools/tf-scale-table.py`'s `REF` dictionary - if it does not belong there, say why in its tooltip.
2. Re-run `python3 tools/tf-scale-table.py` and paste it over the block in section 2.
3. Re-run the gate: `bash tools/pine-lint.sh tools/*.pine`, `python3 tools/pine-validate.py tools/*.pine`,
   `pyne check tools/*.pine`, `python3 tools/pine-gate-run.py tools/*.pine`, `python3 tools/lint.py`.
   The gate's timed run is *itself* an auto-tier run on synthetic daily bars, so it lands on the most
   degenerate row of the table; that is a stress test, not a typical chart, and its `igaps` count will not
   match a 5m chart's. Do not compare its milliseconds across a change to the tier ladder - the
   comparison is meaningless for the same reason `tools/cisd-audit.md` section 14 withdrew the last one.
4. Anything this file claims that is arithmetic rather than measurement (a tier selection, a scaled window,
   a bar-count-to-minutes conversion) can be checked by rerunning the generator. Anything that is a source
   claim keeps its citation in `tools/crt-candle-range-study.md`. Do not launder a source claim into a
   recommendation.
